item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 291756
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Wed Jul 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Genevieve, located several hundred miles west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula. The National
Hurricane Center has issued the last advisory on Post-Tropical
Cyclone Fausto, located a few hundred miles northeast of the
Hawaiian Islands.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Public Advisory Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Wed Jul 29 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 292038
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Genevieve Advisory Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
1100 AM HST Wed Jul 29 2026
 
...GENEVIEVE WEAKENS AS IT MOVES WEST-NORTHWESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 AM HST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.2N 120.1W
ABOUT 705 MI...1135 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...100 MPH...155 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...970 MB...28.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Genevieve was
located near latitude 19.2 North, longitude 120.1 West. Genevieve is
moving toward the west-northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). This general
motion with a slight increase in forward speed is expected during
the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 100 mph (155 km/h)
with higher gusts. Steady weakening is expected during the next
couple of days, and Genevieve is forecast to become post-tropical
this weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 970 mb (28.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Genevieve are affecting portions of the
Baja California Peninsula and will reach Southern California today.
These swells will persist for the next several days and are likely
to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
A depiction of rip current risk for the United States can be found
at: hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams/Beven

item.title: Hurricane Genevieve Forecast Discussion Number 23
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Wed Jul 29 2026 
086 
WTPZ42 KNHC 292042
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Genevieve Discussion Number  23
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP072026
1100 AM HST Wed Jul 29 2026
 
The satellite presentation of Genevieve has slowly deteriorated 
today, as cold cloud top temperatures less than -30 C partially 
obscure the center. A 29/1352Z RCM-2 Synthetic Aperture Radar scan 
revealed that an eyewall replacement cycle had occurred earlier this 
morning and was nearly complete, and subsequently, the radius of 
maximum winds had expanded. Cloud top temperatures in the newly 
formed eyewall are warming, despite the prevalence of deep 
convection. The 1800Z intensity estimate from TAFB was 5.0/90 kt, 
and subjective estimates range from 74-90 kt. Based on these data 
and the satellite presentation, the initial intensity is set at 85 
kt for this advisory.
 
The hurricane is moving toward the west-northwest around 8 kt, along 
the southwestern periphery of a strong mid-level ridge over the 
southern High Plains of the United States. Genevieve is expected to 
continue on a west-northwestward heading through this weekend with 
an increase in forward speed as the ridge expands westward. Late 
this weekend into early next week, Genevieve will turn toward the 
northwest then north, ahead of a strong upper-level low progressing 
eastward over the eastern Pacific. The latest NHC forecast track is 
slightly left of the previous track, and falls in the middle of the 
consensus track guidance, nearest to the corrected (HCCA) consensus 
aid.
 
Genevieve will continue to feel the impacts of moderate 
northwesterly shear over the next 12 h or so, as well as gradually 
cooling waters and unfavorable upper-level dynamics. On Thursday, 
the forecast calls for the hurricane to move into an environment 
with increasingly dry mid-level conditions and waters cooler than 
26C, leading to further weakening. The latest NHC intensity forecast 
has been adjusted further downward during the next 48 h. Genevieve 
is expected to fall below hurricane strength by Thursday night or 
early Friday, and may struggle to produce organized convection by 
the second half of this weekend, as indicated by the GFS and ECMWF.
